sections.h2: Fastest way to sell in Wenatchee
sections.html:
Cash is normally fastest in Wenatchee, since nobody has to wait for an appraisal or a loan to be approved. An agent listing is still worth considering if you can spend time prepping the house and hosting showings.

Wenatchee is Chelan County's seat and biggest city, where the Wenatchee and Columbia rivers join near the eastern foothills of the Cascades. East Wenatchee sits across the Columbia in Douglas County, and the two cities anchor a metro area of about 110,884 people. The city itself has an estimated 35,547 residents.

Median home value is $433,700, with owners in 53.8 percent of homes. The 17.0 minute average commute is a handy selling point, and the city spans about 10.6 square miles of land. Wenatchee calls itself the Apple Capital of the World, and the 10-mile Apple Capital Recreation Loop Trail along both banks of the Columbia draws buyers who like to be outdoors. Mission Ridge is a 30-minute drive for skiing.

sections.h2: Building design numbers and hillside lots
sections.html:
The winters are cold and the summers hot and dry. Keep roof and plumbing records handy, since a buyer will ask about both. The Building Division publishes the design numbers local work must meet:

  • Roof snow load of 40 pounds per square foot
  • Climate zone 5B
  • Design wind speed of 85 mph
  • Footing and foundation freeze depth of 18 inches
  • Waterline depth of at least 3 feet, and 5 feet under a driveway

Houses on the hillsides ringing the city sit against ridges that form a wall on the west and south sides, so slope, drainage and retaining walls deserve attention. Most retaining walls up to four feet high are exempt from a permit, though setbacks and shoreline rules still apply.

The Wenatchee School District provides public K-12 education and serves Malaga, Olds Station, South Wenatchee, Sunnyslope and Wenatchee Heights. It runs seven elementary schools, three middle schools and one high school, Wenatchee High School. Check which attendance area your address falls in before you list.

U.S. Route 2 passes less than a mile north of city limits near Sunnyslope, and U.S. Route 97 also passes north of the city. State Route 28 runs through East Wenatchee across the river. Three bridges cross the Columbia: the Richard Odabashian Bridge and the Senator George Sellar Bridge for vehicles, and the Old Wenatchee Bridge for pedestrians. Link Transit runs buses across Chelan County and into parts of Douglas County.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit before selling?
sections.html:
Only when you do work before the sale. The Building Division's advice is blunt: if you have to ask, you probably need one. A permit covers any building or structure that is erected, constructed, enlarged, altered, repaired, moved, improved, removed, converted or demolished, while painting, papering and similar finish work is exempt.

Also exempt: one-story storage sheds up to 200 square feet kept the required distance from structures and property lines, and decks no higher than 30 inches above grade that do not serve a required exit door. Replacing a leaking sink trap needs no permit, but moving a fixture or installing new drain or supply lines generally does. If a furnace fails, emergency replacement can go ahead right away, though you should get the permit and an inspection once the work is done.

The Building Division is at City Hall, 301 Yakima, and answers at (509) 888-3244, Monday through Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. For rules on short-term rentals or rentals in general, ask Community Development staff or Chelan County before you promise a buyer that use.

sections.h2: How the deed is handled in Chelan County
sections.html:
Any document that conveys property stops at the Chelan County Treasurer before the Auditor records it. There the Real Estate Excise Affidavit is processed and either the excise tax or, for an exempt transaction, a $10 fee is collected. The papers then move on to the Auditor. An exempt transfer still needs the affidavit.

RCW 82.45.090 reinforces the order by blocking recording until the tax is paid or marked not due. Because the tax combines a state and a local part, the Treasurer can tell you what your price owes. Ask early, since the figure is needed before the deed can be recorded and the sale finished.

The Auditor accepts only properly formatted documents with original, notarized signatures and the correct fee. Common reasons for refusal are:

  • A missing parcel number
  • A first-page top margin under 3 inches
  • Illegible text
  • A missing legal description
  • An inadequate fee

sections.h2: Getting the house ready for a buyer
sections.html:
Gather what buyers ask for: roof and plumbing records, permits for anything built or replaced, and notes on hillside drainage or retaining wall work. Did something go in without a permit? The Building Division at (509) 888-3244 can say how to make it compliant.

Then pick your path. Listing reaches the most buyers but demands prep work and showings. Selling for cash gives up reach in exchange for speed, with the buyer accepting the house as is, which helps when repairs look daunting. If the house is a rental, tell buyers early whether a tenant stays, and put what stays with the house in writing so closing day holds no surprises. Collect the receipts and manuals for equipment that stays, and keep a copy of every document you hand to the buyer, the title company or the county. A cash buyer will usually still want to see title cleared before the Treasurer and Auditor steps begin.

sections.h2: The seller disclosure and what to expect
sections.html:
Washington sellers of improved residential property fill out the condition form in RCW 64.06.020, and by default it is due five business days after both sides sign. Disclose problems you know of, such as earlier work done without a permit.

With a cash buyer the sale does not wait on a lender's appraisal, so the schedule depends on title work and the county steps above. Ask each buyer who pays the excise tax, compare what you would net after repairs and carrying costs, and get the closing date in writing. A title or escrow company can carry the affidavit and deed through the Treasurer and the Auditor for you.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Wenatchee house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers often purchase houses as they stand. The state disclosure form in RCW 64.06.020 still goes to the buyer, with any problems you know about listed.

faqs.q: What does the Chelan County Treasurer do in a sale?
faqs.a: The Treasurer processes the Real Estate Excise Affidavit and collects the excise tax due, or a $10 processing fee when the sale is exempt. Only after that does the Auditor record the deed.

faqs.q: Do small projects need a permit in Wenatchee?
faqs.a: Some do not. Painting, certain small sheds, retaining walls up to four feet and low decks are exempt. Moving a plumbing fixture or adding new supply or drain lines generally does require a permit, so call the Building Division at (509) 888-3244.

faqs.q: What snow load and freeze depth apply to Wenatchee homes?
faqs.a: A 40 pound per square foot roof snow load and an 18 inch freeze depth for footings and foundations. The climate zone is 5B, and design wind speed is 85 mph.
